context: Current closing price of Gartner (IT): $192.15 USD as of 2026-11-13.
justification_text:
My point estimates reflect a mild upward drift from what I interpreted as a recent price level around $192–193. At the one-day horizon, the estimate of $192.8 is essentially a near-flat projection, assuming that short-term momentum and market microstructure would keep the price close to its recent close with only marginal drift. At the one-week horizon, I nudged the estimate slightly higher to $193.5, reflecting a modest positive drift assumption consistent with a low-volatility, slow-trending environment. At the one-month horizon, the $195.0 estimate continues that gentle upward drift, anchored loosely to fundamental or macro conditions that I assumed were broadly supportive but not dramatically bullish. All three point estimates are relatively close to one another, which signals that I was not anticipating any strong directional catalyst in the near term.

The confidence interval widths were driven primarily by time-scaling of volatility. For a one-day horizon, a range of roughly $186.5 to $199.1 implies an annualized volatility in the neighborhood of 15–20%, which is consistent with moderate market conditions. As the horizon extends to one week and especially one month, the intervals widen substantially — the one-month range of $172 to $218 spans about 23% of the central estimate — reflecting how uncertainty compounds over time under standard diffusion assumptions. I also factored in that longer horizons are more exposed to regime changes, earnings surprises, macro data, and shifts in sentiment that are simply unknowable at the time of forecasting.

There are several specific risks that could push outcomes outside these stated intervals. On the downside, a sharp deterioration in macroeconomic data, an unexpected credit or liquidity event, geopolitical escalation, or a broader equity market selloff could easily push the one-month outcome below $172. On the upside, a strong earnings beat, a dovish pivot from central banks, or a sudden surge in risk appetite could carry the price well above $218. The one-day interval is the most likely to hold, but even there a surprise news event — a regulatory announcement, a large institutional trade, or an index rebalancing — could breach the bounds. Tail risks, by definition, are underweighted in symmetric confidence intervals, so realized outcomes in stressed conditions could fall meaningfully outside what I stated.
